At 10% progress, prioritize a fixed-weight, cross-fitted transition residual: it is inexpensive to test and directly extends the starting idea. No improvement has yet been measured.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights motivate evidence-based fusion. (1) Directed transitions encode observed next choices. They may distinguish specific follow-ons from broad similarity. (2) Recent anchors emphasize current behavior. They directly target the diagnosis of excessive historical-interest influence. (3) Sparse edges require shrinkage and cross-fitting. Otherwise, isolated transitions and users’ own contributions can create misleading support.

Three literature insights organize the alternatives. (1) TGCL4SR supports combining sequence and transition representations. Its results do not establish gains for this simpler residual. (2) Dirichlet smoothing supplies a principled sparse-row estimate. Popularity normalization measures association, without establishing compatibility or unmet need. (3) gSASRec motivates revisiting sampled prediction objectives. Training margins alone cannot establish generalization.

**Framework and candidate assessment.** The three directions are transition evidence, adaptive temporal fusion, and ranking objectives. Scores below are prospective judgments; O/P/U/M/D denote originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty, each 0–10; higher D means harder.

| Idea | O/P/U/M/D | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed recent transition residual | 5/7/8/7/3 | O: useful synthesis, established ingredients; P: reusable evidence channel, sparse coverage; U: targets specificity and recency, cannot identify fulfilled needs; M: may repair wrong pairs, may introduce errors; D: sparse counts suffice, scoring adapters require care. |
| Support-aware recent-history gate | 5/7/8/7/5 | O: combines timing and support, familiar gating; P: adapts evidence strength, overfitting risk; U: responds to recent interests, intent remains latent; M: may protect weak rows, calibration is uncertain; D: small network, cross-fitted fitting adds complexity. |
| Uniform multi-negative cross-entropy | 3/7/4/8/4 | O: established objective, little novelty; P: scalable baseline, dataset-dependent gains; U: sharper ranking, weak recency mechanism; M: directly targets separation, uncertain negatives remain; D: encoder unchanged, sampling needs safeguards. |

**Selected algorithm.** For each category, partition training users deterministically into folds. Excluding each fold, estimate adjacent-transition counts and a strictly positive, smoothed destination prior. Set p(j|i)=(c_ij+αq_j)/(n_i+α). Average clipped log(p(j|i)/q_j) across the last K nonpadding items with fixed recency weights, then add λ times this residual to SASRec scores. All transforms are independent of the candidate set.

This explicitly targets broad matches displacing specific choices and historical interests outweighing recent intent. It also targets observed wrong-pair rankings, especially Electronics and CDs, without claiming redundancy detection.

```python
for fold in training_user_folds:
    tables[fold] = count_and_smooth(users_excluding(fold))
residual = recent_transition_evidence(sequence, candidates, tables)
scores = sasrec_scores + weight * residual
```

idea.description: Add a fixed-weight, recent directed-transition residual to each category's SASRec. Estimate popularity-smoothed transition probabilities from training histories and combine their clipped log association ratios with neural scores.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies overly broad matches and excessive historical-interest influence. Recent directed evidence offers a testable response to both. Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl also have the highest supplied training-pair error rates, motivating paired residual-on/off analysis without assuming validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep all four independent category models and routing. Use only training interactions for transition counts and popularity estimates. Cross-fit by entire users whenever fitting or diagnosing residual fusion on training examples; exclude the scored user's fold from both counts and priors. Smooth destination popularity to positive support over the catalog, exclude padding, and use candidate-independent clipping and fixed recency weights. Begin with a small prespecified sweep over alpha, recent-window size, and residual weight including zero; retain the common macro validation HR@10 criterion and account for every trial's GPU cost. For deployment, rebuild support from all training users and serialize sparse tables and fusion settings beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reproduces scoring. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Keep view.model as the actual nn.Module and preserve compatibility methods; features must retain recent item IDs explicitly for residual scoring. Provide view.predict_score_base and use excluded-fold support for paired training diagnostics. Keep unavailable metadata and simulator traits unobserved. These associations cannot establish compatibility, redundancy, ownership, or unmet need.
idea.pseudocode:
def build_support(training_users, excluded_fold=None):
    histories = users_outside_fold(training_users, excluded_fold)
    counts = adjacent_directed_counts(histories)
    q = positive_smoothed_destination_frequency(histories)
    return counts, row_sums(counts), q

def residual(sequence, candidates, support, alpha, K, clip):
    counts, totals, q = support
    anchors, weights = last_K_nonpadding_with_fixed_recency_weights(sequence, K)
    result = zeros_like_candidates(candidates)
    for i, w in zip(anchors, weights):
        p = (counts[i, candidates] + alpha*q[candidates]) / (totals[i] + alpha)
        result += w * clamp(log(p / q[candidates]), -clip, clip)
    return result

# Training-pair fitting/diagnosis: use support excluding the user's entire fold.
# Validation/deployment: use support built from all training users.
scores = sasrec_scores(sequence, candidates) + lambda_ * residual(sequence, candidates, support, alpha, K, clip)

originality.positive: Combines recent directed association, popularity-centered shrinkage, and user-level cross-fitting in a minimal SASRec extension.
originality.negative: Transition fusion, smoothing, and out-of-fold estimation are established techniques; novelty lies mainly in their combination.

future_potential.positive: Creates an interpretable evidence channel that can later support uncertainty-aware temporal gating.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transition coverage and shifts in user behavior may limit gains; aggregate benchmark improvements would not establish satisfaction.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires sparse counting and score fusion while retaining the trained SASRec encoder.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct cross-fitting, sequence-aware diagnostic features, and identical deployed scoring require careful integration.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR: Temporal Graph Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models temporal item-transition graphs, motivating sequence and transition evidence as complementary representations.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of the proposed count-based residual on this benchmark.

related_work.title: A Study of Smoothing Methods for Language Models Applied to Ad Hoc Information Retrieval
contributions: Provides the Dirichlet smoothing foundation for shrinking sparse conditional distributions toward a background prior.
limitations: Recommendation transitions require separate validation; smoothing does not identify practical compatibility or causal preference.

related_work.title: Out-of-fold stacking reference supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates constructing fusion features without using the scored observation's training contribution.
limitations: User-level transition cross-fitting is a proposed adaptation; deployment tables include more training users than excluded-fold tables.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Identifies sampled-BCE overconfidence and introduces generalized BCE, motivating an objective-focused alternative.
limitations: Does not directly address recent directed evidence or establish why the supplied Electronics and CDs training pairs fail.
